```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
import re
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.express as px

from pathlib import Path
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, split, explode, regexp_replace, transform, when
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, monotonically_increasing_id

np.random.seed(42)

import plotly.io as pio
pio.renderers.default = "notebook"
#pio.renderers.default = "plotly_mimetype"

from IPython.display import display, HTML

# Initialize Spark Session
spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("CareerCompassData").getOrCreate()

def spark_to_pandas(sdf):
    rows = [row.asDict(recursive=True) for row in sdf.collect()]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=sdf.columns)

OUTPUT_DIR = Path("output")

def export_plotly_figure(fig, name, width=1000, height=800, scale=1):
    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    html_path = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{name}.html"
    svg_path = OUTPUT_DIR / f"{name}.svg"

    try:
        html = pio.to_html(fig, full_html=True, include_plotlyjs="cdn")
        html_path.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"HTML export skipped for {name}: {exc}")

    try:
        fig.write_image(str(svg_path.resolve()), width=width, height=height, scale=scale)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Static SVG export skipped for {name}: {exc}")

# Load Data (all 17 Parquet partition files)
from pathlib import Path
data_dir = Path("../Jobs_2026").resolve() 
df = spark.read.parquet(*[path.as_uri() for path in sorted(data_dir.glob("*.parquet"))])
df.createOrReplaceTempView("job_postings")

# Show Schema and Sample Data
#print("---This is Diagnostic check, No need to print it in the final doc---")
#df.printSchema() # comment this line when rendering the submission

#df.show(5)
#spark.sql("SELECT * FROM job_postings LIMIT 5").toPandas()


#Use SALARY directly if it's a valid non-zero number
#Calclate Average of SALARY_FROM + SALARY_TO if both are valid
#Default to whichever single field is available
#Default to NULL if all three are missing/empty/zero

cleaned_df = spark.sql("""
    WITH base AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT
            ID,
            NAICS2_NAME,
            CASE 
              WHEN lower(trim(EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME)) like '%temp%' OR lower(trim(EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME)) = '%temporary%' THEN 'Temporary'
              WHEN lower(trim(EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME)) like '%part%' OR lower(trim(EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME)) in ('Part-time', 'PART_TIME', 'Part Time') THEN 'Part-Time'
              WHEN lower(trim(EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME)) like '%full%' OR lower(trim(EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME)) in ('Full-time', 'full_time', 'Full-Time') THEN 'Full-Time'
              ELSE 'Other'
            end as EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME_CLEAN,
            REGEXP_REPLACE(EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME, '[\\n\\r]', ' ') AS EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME_CLEAN,
            REMOTE_TYPE_NAME,
            MAX_YEARS_EXPERIENCE,
            ONET_NAME,
            SALARY_FROM,
            SALARY_TO,
            SALARY,
            CASE
                WHEN SALARY IS NOT NULL
                     AND SALARY != ''
                     AND TRY_CAST(SALARY AS DOUBLE) > 0
                    THEN TRY_CAST(SALARY AS DOUBLE)
                WHEN TRY_CAST(SALARY_FROM AS DOUBLE) > 0
                     AND TRY_CAST(SALARY_TO AS DOUBLE) > 0
                    THEN (TRY_CAST(SALARY_FROM AS DOUBLE) + TRY_CAST(SALARY_TO AS DOUBLE)) / 2.0
                WHEN TRY_CAST(SALARY_FROM AS DOUBLE) > 0
                    THEN TRY_CAST(SALARY_FROM AS DOUBLE)
                WHEN TRY_CAST(SALARY_TO AS DOUBLE) > 0
                    THEN TRY_CAST(SALARY_TO AS DOUBLE)
                ELSE NULL
            END AS SALARY_IMPUTED
        FROM job_postings
    ),
    -- Flatten rows where data is enum (Education, Employment Type)
    expanded AS (
        SELECT
            b.ID,
            b.NAICS2_NAME,
            TRIM(emp_type) AS EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME_CLEAN,
            TRIM(edu_level) AS EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME_CLEAN,
            b.REMOTE_TYPE_NAME,
            b.MAX_YEARS_EXPERIENCE,
            b.ONET_NAME,
            b.SALARY_FROM,
            b.SALARY_TO,
            b.SALARY,
            b.SALARY_IMPUTED
        FROM base b
        -- flatten comma-separated employment types into individual rows
        LATERAL VIEW OUTER EXPLODE(SPLIT(b.EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME_CLEAN, ',')) e AS emp_type
        -- flatten JSON array of education levels into individual rows
        LATERAL VIEW OUTER EXPLODE(FROM_JSON(
            b.EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME_CLEAN, 'ARRAY<STRING>'
        )) d AS edu_level
        WHERE b.SALARY_IMPUTED > 0
    )
    SELECT
        *,
        -- if SALARY_IMPUTED is an hourly rate (< $1,000) then annualise it
        -- threshold: $1,000 < lowest plausible annual; × 2,080 = 40 hrs × 52 wks
        CASE
            WHEN SALARY_IMPUTED < 1000 THEN ROUND(SALARY_IMPUTED * 2080, 0)
            ELSE SALARY_IMPUTED
        END AS SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL
    FROM expanded
""")


cleaned_df.createOrReplaceTempView("job_postings_clean")
cleaned_df.toPandas().to_csv("salary_cleaned.csv", index=False)
spark.sql("SELECT * FROM job_postings_clean LIMIT 5").toPandas()
```

# Salary Distribution by Industry and Employment Type
```{python}

salary_pd = spark.sql("""
    SELECT
        NAICS2_NAME,
        EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME_CLEAN,
        TRY_CAST(SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL AS DOUBLE) AS SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL
    FROM job_postings_clean
    WHERE TRY_CAST(SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL AS DOUBLE) > 1000
      AND NAICS2_NAME IS NOT NULL
      AND EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME_CLEAN IS NOT NULL
""").toPandas()

# remove 99th pct outliers - e.g. some annual salaries are over 100M USD
p99 = salary_pd["SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL"].quantile(0.99)
salary_pd = salary_pd[salary_pd["SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL"] <= p99]

fig = px.box(
    salary_pd,
    x="NAICS2_NAME",
    y="SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL",
    color="EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME_CLEAN",
    title="Salary Distribution by Industry and Employment Type",
    labels={
        "NAICS2_NAME": "Industry (NAICS2)",
        "SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL": "Starting Salary (USD)",
        "EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME_CLEAN": "Employment Type",
    },
    points=False,
)

fig.update_layout(
    height=600,
    font=dict(family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif", size=12),
    title_font=dict(size=15, color="#0b0b0b"),
    plot_bgcolor="#fcfcfb",
    paper_bgcolor="#fcfcfb",
    xaxis=dict(tickangle=-40, tickfont=dict(size=9, color="#52514e"), showgrid=False, linecolor="#c3c2b7"),
    yaxis=dict(tickformat="$,.0f", gridcolor="#e1e0d9", linecolor="#c3c2b7", zeroline=False),
    legend=dict(title_text="Employment Type", orientation="h", y=-0.55, x=0, font=dict(size=10)),
    margin=dict(t=60, b=260, l=90, r=20),
)

## The median salary for most industries falls within the USD 100,000 to 200,000 range.
#fig.show(renderer="plotly_mimetype")
display(HTML(fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs="cdn")))

```


#  Salary Analysis by ONET Occupation Type (Bubble Chart)
## TBD
```{python}

onet_pd = spark.sql("""
    SELECT
        ONET_NAME AS Occupation_Name,
        PERCENTILE(SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL, 0.5) AS Median_Salary,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ID) AS Job_Postings
    FROM job_postings_clean
    WHERE SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL IS NOT NULL
      AND SALARY_IMPUTED_ANNUAL > 1000
      AND ONET_NAME IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ONET_NAME
    ORDER BY Job_Postings DESC
""").toPandas()

fig = px.scatter(
    onet_pd,
    x="Occupation_Name",
    y="Median_Salary",
    size="Job_Postings",
    color="Job_Postings",
    color_continuous_scale="Viridis",
    title="Median Salary by ONET Occupation",
    labels={
        "Occupation_Name": "ONET Occupation",
        "Median_Salary": "Median Salary",
        "Job_Postings": "Number of Met Career Compass records",
    },
    size_max=80,
)

fig.update_layout(
    height=600,
    font=dict(family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif", size=12),
    title_font=dict(size=15, color="#0b0b0b"),
    plot_bgcolor="#fcfcfb",
    paper_bgcolor="#fcfcfb",
    xaxis=dict(
        title="ONET Occupation",
        tickangle=-40,
        tickfont=dict(size=10, color="#52514e"),
        showgrid=False,
        linecolor="#c3c2b7",
    ),
    yaxis=dict(
        title="Median Salary",
        tickformat="$,.0f",
        tickfont=dict(size=11),
        gridcolor="#e1e0d9",
        linecolor="#c3c2b7",
        zeroline=False,
    ),
    coloraxis_colorbar=dict(
        title="Number of Met Career<br>Compass records",
        tickformat=",",
        thickness=15,
        len=0.75,
    ),
    margin=dict(t=60, b=200, l=90, r=120),
)

display(HTML(fig.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs="cdn")))
```
